title: Which digit decides the rounding?
text: Hundredths is the second digit after the decimal point. In $$4.268$$ that digit is 6, and the next digit (thousandths) decides whether 6 stays or goes up. A common mistake is to look at the tenths digit, or to round 6 using the 4 in front. What is the thousandths digit?

title: Does 6 go up?
text: The deciding digit is 5 or more, so the hundredths digit increases by 1. What is $$6 + 1$$?

title: Worked solution
text: $$4.268$$ to the nearest hundredth is $$4.27$$. The thousandths digit 8 tells you to round the 6 up. Common mistake: answering $$4.26$$ (truncating) or $$4.3$$ (rounding to tenths). General rule: find the place you are keeping, look one place to the right, and round up when that digit is 5, 6, 7, 8, or 9.
